title: Use timing model: item animation vs item time (swings never restart, real bursts)
player_outcome: Pickaxes, axes and swords always finish their swing: holding a pickaxe reads as one smooth continuous chop while tiles are hit on the tool's own cadence. Melee-speed accessories and speed prefixes make the whole swing faster, not just the cooldown. The Clockwork Assault Rifle fires a real 3-round burst. The cursor's reach finally includes reach bonuses (Builder Potion).
design: Verified: ItemUseSystem.cs:161-162 sets UseCooldown=useTime and UseAnimation=item.UseAnimation on every use. PlayerAvatar.Motion.cs:194 replays when UseAnimation jumps back up, so copper pickaxe (15/21) restarts at 71%. Speed stats divide useTime only (lines 97, 110, 158). MeleeSystem.cs:51 uses unscaled item.UseAnimation. InteractionController.cs:101 ignores the Reach stat.

Pre-split for the 400-line cap, with no behaviour change, and run the tests. Move PlayerEntity out of src/Strata.Core/Session/GameWorld.cs (387 lines) into Session/PlayerEntity.cs. Split ItemUseSystem.cs (375 lines) three ways: ItemUseSystem.cs (Use, UseTool, Place, anchors), ItemUseSystem.Shooting.cs (Shoot, FindAmmo) and ItemUseSystem.Consume.cs (Consume, Summon, StartEvent, ConsumeHeld).

PlayerEntity: UseCooldown is Terraria's itemTime and UseAnimation its itemAnimation. Add three fields. UseAnimationMax is the effective length of the current animation. UseSerial is an int that goes up by 1 whenever a new animation starts; all presentation keys off it. ReuseDelay counts ticks before the next animation may start.
ItemDef: add ReuseDelay (ticks, default 0; Terraria reuseDelay).

New Core UseTiming.For(ItemStack, ItemUseInfo, StatSheet) returns (Animation, Time). The prefix UseSpeed divides both. MeleeSpeed divides both for Melee/Thrust weapons that are not tools. MiningSpeed divides Time only, for tools. Both are clamped to at least 1. Also add UseTiming.ReachMeters(PlayerEntity, ItemDef) = (item.Reach + Reach stat) * CellSize.

ItemUseSystem.Use, mid-animation (UseAnimation > 0): return Cooldown unless UseCooldown == 0 and the item repeats within an animation (tools; shooters with Time < Animation). If it does, act again (UseTool or Shoot) without touching UseAnimation or UseSerial and without raising Swung.

ItemUseSystem.Use, idle: respect ReuseDelay, then perform the action. Only on success, start an animation: set UseAnimation = UseAnimationMax = Animation, increment UseSerial, set UseCooldown = Time, and raise Swung for melee. Failed outcomes start nothing.

Add ItemUseSystem.Continue(PlayerEntity), called from GameWorld.TickPlayer. When the player is mid-animation with UseCooldown 0 and holds a burst shooter, it fires the next shot without input: a started burst always completes, as in Terraria.
GameWorld.TickPlayer: decrement UseCooldown, UseAnimation and ReuseDelay. When UseAnimation hits 0, set ReuseDelay = held.ReuseDelay. Then call ItemUse.Continue(p).

Game side: PlayerAvatar.Motion plays the action when UseSerial changes, over UseAnimationMax/60 s. ViewModel phase t = 1 - (UseAnimation - Engine.GetPhysicsInterpolationFraction())/UseAnimationMax (smooth, no one-frame snap). SwingTrail duration = UseAnimationMax/60. InteractionController.UpdateTarget uses UseTiming.ReachMeters so the cursor, ghost and cracks agree with the use.
Commands and probes: the 'use' command also clears UseAnimation and ReuseDelay. Add probes player.swings (UseSerial) and player.use_anim.
